name: AMORLINC
description: AMORLINC returns the straight-line depreciation of an asset for a given period, commonly used in French accounting.
tldr: Calculates depreciation for a specific period using the French straight-line method.

parameters.name: first_period
parameters.description: End date of the first period.

parameters.name: salvage
parameters.description: Salvage value at the end of the asset life.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Period for which to calculate depreciation.

basicExample.explanation: Calculates first-year straight-line depreciation for a $10,000 asset with a 20% rate.

howItWorks: AMORLINC calculates depreciation by dividing the depreciable amount by the asset life. It is the French straight-line equivalent.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Used mainly in French accounting standards.
First and last periods may be prorated based on the basis.

commonErrors.fix: Verify dates and period are valid.

commonErrors.cause: Rate does not match the expected straight-line rate.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: AMORLINC works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between AMORLINC and AMORDEGRC?
faq.answer: AMORLINC uses straight-line depreciation. AMORDEGRC uses declining balance.

faq.question: When is AMORLINC used?
faq.answer: It is used in French accounting for straight-line depreciation.
